# Electrolytes for long runs

## Why I care
At work I've seen a marathoner come in confused and vomiting after drinking water at every station, sodium 126. Exercise-associated hyponatremia is real and it's mostly from overdrinking plain water, not from sweating out too much salt. So my rule: drink to thirst, and the fluid I drink has sodium in it.

Also my own lesson: 2025-07-26, 28 km at 29°C and humid, plain water only, white salt crust on the cap, cramping calves from km 22 and a migraine that night ([[Migraine triggers]]).

## Sweat test
2025-06-14 at Runner's Lab Etobicoke, $129, ref RL-40926. Patch sweat test plus a weighed 60 min run on the treadmill at 24°C:
- sweat sodium: **1,050 mg/L** (they said "moderately salty")
- sweat rate: **0.9 L/h** at 24°C, probably 1.2 L/h in real summer humidity
- so about 950 mg sodium lost per hour in mild weather

## Products I've tried
| product | sodium | notes |
|---|---|---|
| Nuun Sport tab | 300 mg / tab | fizzy, tastes fine, lemon lime best |
| LMNT stick | 1,000 mg | too salty to drink fast, good the night before |
| SaltStick Caps | 215 mg / cap | easy, swallow with water |
| Maurten Drink Mix 160 | 200 mg / 500 ml | expensive, $4.20 a serving |
| Gatorade on course | ~230 mg / 500 ml | what the race gives out |
| pickle juice shot | ~400 mg / 60 ml | gross but works for cramps |

## The plan for runs over 90 minutes
- before: 500 ml with 1 Nuun tab, 60 min before
- during: 500 to 700 ml per hour, each 500 ml with one Nuun tab, plus 1 SaltStick cap per hour when it's above 20°C
- target roughly 600 to 800 mg sodium per hour, not chasing the full 950
- gels every 35 min for carbs (they have a little sodium too, Maurten Gel 100 has 34 mg, basically nothing)
- after: salty food, chocolate milk, weigh myself, drink 1.5 × what I lost

## Hydration vest
Salomon Active Skin 8, size S, two 500 ml soft flasks. $180 at Sporting Life, bought 2025-05-30. No bounce. Holds 4 gels, phone, keys, Nuun tube.

## Race day (2025-10-19)
Forecast for Toronto was 9°C at the start, so less sweat. Plan:
- no vest, carry one 500 ml flask with 1 Nuun, refill at km 21 from the Gatorade station
- 3 SaltStick caps in the shorts pocket, take one at 1:30, 2:30, 3:30
- Gatorade at about every second station, water when the gel goes down
- more on the gel timing and pace in [[Marathon taper]]

## Mistakes so far
1. 2025-06-28: took 2 SaltStick caps without water, stomach cramp
2. 2025-08-09: forgot the Nuun tube, used a gas station Gatorade, fine actually
3. 2025-09-13: LMNT during a run, way too salty, gagged at km 14

## Off-season
Way less matters for runs under 75 minutes. Normal food covers it. The flu in January was the exception, electrolytes helped then too ([[感冒与流感]]).

Related: [[Couch to 5k]] for the early days when I thought a sip of water at the end was plenty.
